false_assurance_claims: - Absolute names and `..` names are rejected. A name containing a NUL byte would fail at write time and could leave a partial write (the docs concede there is no rollback). — Blanket rejection of absolute entry names is too broad: an absolute destination already inside the workspace resolves to an allowed suffix. The actual guard rejects escapes.

- **Node 20 `--unhandled-rejections`** (official docs, 2026-10-24): the default mode throws on an unhandled rejection. I found no unhandled-rejection path, since `reply` in the catch block cannot practically throw. — Supplied evidence does not prove reply in the catch cannot throw or encounter response errors. This categorical rationale exceeds a bounded no-path-found assessment.
